requirement: Summarise many documents in parallel with a LangGraph-like Send fan-out and an operator.add reducer, keeping worker payloads private and the merged result in input order.
skeleton: A fan-out limit, a frozen Send dataclass, a fan_out function building one Send per document, and a MapReduceGraph whose invoke runs workers, reduces with operator.add, orders by index and joins the summaries.
caption: A LangGraph-style map-reduce fan-out written in the standard library with operator, functools reduce, dataclasses and typing and no third-party imports. Send is a frozen dataclass of node name and arg. fan_out raises ValueError past MAX_FANOUT of 32 documents and returns one Send to summarize per document whose arg holds only that doc and its index, never the rest of the state. MapReduceGraph.invoke raises ValueError for a Send to an unknown node, runs the worker for each Send to get a one-item summaries list of index and text, merges the lists with reduce and operator.add starting from an empty list, orders them by index, and returns a new state with summaries and final joined by newlines or (no documents) when empty. The fixture asserts private payloads, document order, kept duplicates, no workers for empty input, an unmutated input and the inclusive fan-out limit.

plan.intent: Summarise a batch of documents for a report
constraints: Each worker receives only its document and index
A Send to an unknown node raises ValueError
Merged summaries follow the input order and keep duplicates
Empty input runs no workers and reports no documents

rationale.teaches: Fan out with one Send per item carrying a minimal payload, then fold the partial updates with an operator.add reducer and restore order by index.
rationale.why: Passing the whole state to workers leaks data and bloats payloads, and merging by completion or content order scrambles or drops results.

ops.docstring: A LangGraph-style map-reduce step that fans out with Send objects.

candidates.why_wrong: Every worker receives the full graph state instead of only its own document.
A batch of exactly 32 documents is rejected although the limit allows it.
Summaries are sorted alphabetically, losing the order of the input documents.
Identical summaries are deduplicated so duplicate documents lose their entries.
An empty batch produces an empty final string instead of the no documents marker.
